graderOnly: README.md still shows the old `tag=` filter syntax in its Searching and Saved searches examples and states that saved searches keep working when you upgrade notes.

Since the correction for implementation.md#F-002 (src/query.js now rejects every `tag=` token), a saved search stored before the upgrade with the old syntax fails with exit status 2 when run with `notes saved run`, so the README upgrade promise is false for existing saved searches.

The scope assumes existing saved searches do not use the `tag=` form; the README's own saved-search example and its upgrade promise show that assumption is false. Whether old saved searches must keep working, be migrated, or may break is therefore an open Scoper-owned behavior decision, so Documenter cannot settle the README text by itself.
docs/guide.md still describes the old `tag=` syntax; updating it for AC-004 is Documenter's own work and needs no other owner.
No documentation record exists for the cycle before the run.
The implementation matches the scope and design as written; there is no implementation or verification defect to route.

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 00-project (pre-install): a small Node CLI, notes, that searches a JSON notes export, with the old tag=<name> filter, saved searches stored as raw query text, README.md (old syntax plus the promise that saved searches keep working across upgrades), docs/guide.md (old syntax), and tests. 50-scope: Auditor context, scope (AC-001 filters, AC-002 phrases, AC-003 reject old tag= form with exit 2, AC-004 user guide; non-goal about the saved.json format, nothing about old-syntax saved queries), design, STATE at DEVELOPING. 51-implement: src/query.js first version (old-form check only at query start), search.js, CLI exit 2, plan, STATE TESTING. 52-verify: Tester tests and VERIFY report, STATE REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION. 53-fix: query.js checks every token, plan notes reopening DEV-002 for implementation.md#F-002. 54-reverify: added test and REVERIFY report. 55-review: implementation review COMPLETE with F-001 WITHDRAWN and F-002 RESOLVED (README and guide excluded as documentation-phase work), STATE DOCUMENTING with FORWARD from REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION and no recovery. No documentation record exists. The F-002 correction is exactly what makes old saved searches fail, which ties the README discrepancy to F-002. Compromises: commits carry the default 2026-09-24 date although the given cycle id is stamped 2026-09-27; the recovery round for F-002 (DEVELOPING and TESTING reruns) is not reflected in intermediate STATE commits, only in the records.
